claim: MRP1 is an ABC exporter that extrudes a variety of chemotherapeutic agents and native substrates.
source: Multidrug resistance protein 1 (MRP1) is an ABC exporter that extrudes a variety of chemotherapeutic agents and native substrates.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the function of MRP1.

claim: Structures of MRP1 were previously determined in an inward-facing (IF) or outward-facing (OF) conformation.
source: Previously, the structures of MRP1 were determined in an inward-facing (IF) or outward-facing (OF) conformation.
evidence: This statement references prior structural work on MRP1.

claim: Substrate stimulates ATP hydrolysis by accelerating the IF-to-OF transition.
source: Our results show that substrate stimulates ATP hydrolysis by accelerating the IF-to-OF transition.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The rate-limiting step of the transport cycle is the dissociation of the nucleotide-binding-domain dimer.
source: The rate-limiting step of the transport cycle is the dissociation of the nucleotide-binding-domain dimer, while ATP hydrolysis per se does not reset MRP1 to the resting state.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by both smFRET and cryo-EM data.

claim: ATP hydrolysis per se does not reset MRP1 to the resting state.
source: The rate-limiting step of the transport cycle is the dissociation of the nucleotide-binding-domain dimer, while ATP hydrolysis per se does not reset MRP1 to the resting state.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural data showing no conformational change upon ATP hydrolysis.

claim: Native substrates of MRP1 include a variety of antioxidants, pro-inflammatory molecules, and hormones.
source: Native substrates of MRP1 include a variety of antioxidants, pro-inflammatory molecules, and hormones (Cole and Deeley, 2006; Deeley and Cole, 2006; Deeley et al., 2006; Leslie et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: MRP1 transports a number of chemotherapeutic agents, thereby conferring drug resistance in multiple cancer types.
source: MRP1 also transports a number of chemotherapeutic agents, thereby conferring drug resistance in acute myeloblastic and lymphoblastic leukemia, non-small-cell lung cancer, prostate cancer, breast cancer, and neuroblastoma (Berger et al., 2005; Cole, 2014b; Filipits et al., 2005; Haber et al., 2006; Winter et al., 2013; Zalcberg et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: MRP1 is a single polypeptide comprising three transmembrane domains (TMD0, TMD1, and TMD2) and two cytosolic nucleotide-binding domains (NBD1 and NBD2).
source: MRP1 is a single polypeptide comprising three transmembrane domains (TMD0, TMD1, and TMD2) and two cytosolic nucleotide-binding domains (NBD1 and NBD2).
evidence: This is a structural description of MRP1 based on established knowledge.

claim: Structures of bovine MRP1 (bMRP1) have been determined by electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) in three functional states.
source: Structures of bovine MRP1 (bMRP1) have been determined by electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) in three functional states (Johnson and Chen, 2017; Johnson and Chen, 2018): an apo form in the absence of substrate and ATP, a complex with the native substrate leukotriene C4 (LTC4) in the absence of ATP, and a structure of the hydrolysis-deficient E1454Q mutant determined in the presence of both LTC4 and ATP (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement references prior structural work and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In the absence of ATP, MRP1 adopts an inward-facing (IF) conformation, in which the two NBDs are widely separated and the translocation pathway is open to the cytoplasm.
source: In the absence of ATP, MRP1 adopts an inward-facing (IF) conformation, in which the two NBDs are widely separated and the translocation pathway is open to the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a structural description based on prior cryo-EM structures.

claim: Binding of LTC4 at the center of the membrane, between TMD1 and TMD2, brings the two halves of the transporter closer together.
source: Binding of LTC4 at the center of the membrane, between TMD1 and TMD2, brings the two halves of the transporter closer together.
evidence: This is a structural observation from prior cryo-EM work.

claim: Upon binding of ATP, the transporter adopts its fully NBD-closed configuration concurrent with opening of the translocation pathway to the outside.
source: Upon binding of ATP, the transporter adopts its fully NBD-closed configuration concurrent with opening of the translocation pathway to the outside.
evidence: This is a structural observation from prior cryo-EM work.

claim: In the outward-facing (OF) conformation, the LTC4-binding pocket becomes deformed, no longer competent to bind substrate.
source: Meanwhile, the LTC4-binding pocket becomes deformed, no longer competent to bind substrate.
evidence: This is a structural observation from prior cryo-EM work.

claim: In the OF conformation, two ATP molecules are occluded at the NBD dimer interface: one in the catalytically inactive, degenerate site and the other in the active consensus site, poised for hydrolysis.
source: In this outward-facing (OF) conformation, two ATP molecules are occluded at the NBD dimer interface: one in the catalytically inactive, degenerate site and the other in the active consensus site, poised for hydrolysis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from prior cryo-EM work, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Fluorescently labeled bMRP1 hydrolyzed ATP at rates virtually identical to those of the unmodified WT protein.
source: In solution, the fluorescently labeled bMRP1 hydrolyzed ATP at rates virtually identical to those of the unmodified WT protein (Figure 1B and C), indicating that insertion of the peptide tags and incorporation of the fluorophores did not alter the kinetics of bMRP1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Insertion of the peptide tags and incorporation of the fluorophores did not alter the kinetics of bMRP1.
source: In solution, the fluorescently labeled bMRP1 hydrolyzed ATP at rates virtually identical to those of the unmodified WT protein (Figure 1B and C), indicating that insertion of the peptide tags and incorporation of the fluorophores did not alter the kinetics of bMRP1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that labeled and unlabeled proteins have identical ATP hydrolysis rates.

claim: In the absence of ATP and substrate (apo), the FRET histogram showed a broad distribution of E values spanning from 0.2 to 0.9.
source: In the absence of ATP and substrate (apo), the FRET histogram showed a broad distribution of E values spanning from 0.2 to 0.9.
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments.

claim: Saturating concentrations of LTC4 (10 µM) or ATP (5 mM) shifted the FRET distribution towards higher E values.
source: Saturating concentrations of LTC4 (10 µM) or ATP (5 mM) shifted the FRET distribution towards higher E values.
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments.

claim: When both LTC4 and ATP were present, a predominant high FRET peak emerged.
source: When both LTC4 and ATP were present, a predominant high FRET peak emerged.
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments.

claim: Addition of ATP and LTC4 together with orthovanadate (Vi), a hydrolysis transition-state analogue, further promoted the high FRET state.
source: Addition of ATP and LTC4 together with orthovanadate (Vi), a hydrolysis transition-state analogue, further promoted the high FRET state (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The FRET distribution for the E1454Q mutant in the presence of ATP and LTC4 was dominated by a high FRET state.
source: The FRET distribution for the E1454Q mutant in the presence of ATP and LTC4 was also dominated by a high FRET state (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A five-state model with mean FRET values of 0.23, 0.42, 0.63, 0.80, and 0.92 was identified to describe the FRET distributions.
source: To quantitatively characterize the FRET distributions, we applied the empirical Bayesian method implemented in ebFRET (van de Meent et al., 2014) and identified a common set of five FRET states, with mean E values of 0.23, 0.42, 0.63, 0.80, and 0.92.
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of smFRET data using ebFRET.

claim: The FRET distributions obtained under all experimental conditions can be described as combinations of the five states.
source: The FRET distributions obtained under all above experimental conditions can be described as combinations of the five states (Figure 2A, lower panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fitting the data to the five-state model as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A four-state model is insufficient to describe transitions observed in the FRET trajectories.
source: A four-state model is insufficient to describe transitions observed in the FRET trajectories (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by model comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The occupancy of the E = 0.80 state increased monotonically as the LTC4 concentration was raised.
source: The occupancy of the E = 0.80 state increased monotonically as the LTC4 concentration was raised, whereas those of the other states did not (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), consistent with the peak position of 0.8 from the overall FRET distribution collected at saturating LTC4 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 2B and supplementary figures.

claim: The half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) of LTC4 for the E = 0.80 state occupancy is 0.32 ± 0.17 µM.
source: The half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) of LTC4 for the E = 0.80 state occupancy is 0.32 ± 0.17 µM, in agreement with the LTC4 concentration required for half-maximal stimulation of ATP hydrolysis measured in a bulk ATPase assay (0.35 ± 0.09 µM) (Johnson and Chen, 2017).
evidence: This is determined from dose-response analysis of smFRET data and agrees with bulk ATPase assay results.

claim: The E = 0.80 state (termed IF1) corresponds to the inward-facing cryo-EM structure determined in the presence of saturating LTC4.
source: Therefore we rationalized that the E = 0.80 state (termed IF1) corresponds to the inward-facing cryo-EM structure determined in the presence of saturating LTC4 (Figure 1A, middle).
evidence: This assignment is based on the correlation between LTC4 binding and the E = 0.80 state occupancy, and agreement with prior structural data.

claim: The E = 0.92 state indicates a conformation in which the NBDs are in closer proximity than that of the LTC4-bound structure.
source: The highest FRET state (E = 0.92) indicates a conformation in which the NBDs are in closer proximity than that of the LTC4-bound structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the FRET efficiency value, which is higher than the IF1 state.

claim: The occupancy of the E = 0.92 state increased as a function of ATP concentration.
source: Its occupancy increased as a function of ATP concentration, but those of the lower FRET states did not (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and D), consistent with visual inspection of the overall FRET distribution (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 2C and supplementary figures.

claim: The E1454Q mutant predominately occupied the E = 0.92 state at saturating concentrations of ATP and LTC4.
source: Moreover, the E1454Q mutant predominately occupied the E = 0.92 state at saturating concentrations of ATP and LTC4 (Figure 2A), similar to the condition under which the cryo-EM structure of the outward-facing conformation was determined (Johnson and Chen, 2018).
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The E = 0.92 state corresponds to the OF conformation.
source: These observations support a direct correspondence between the E = 0.92 state and the OF conformation.
evidence: This assignment is based on ATP-dependent occupancy and correlation with the E1454Q mutant structure.

claim: The three lowest FRET states (E = 0.63, 0.42, and 0.23) indicate conformations in which the NBDs are further separated than in the LTC4-bound structure.
source: The three lowest FRET states (i.e., E = 0.63, 0.42, and 0.23) indicate conformations in which the NBDs are further separated than in the LTC4-bound structure, and thus are presumably ligand-free and inward-facing (termed IF2, IF3, and IF4, respectively).
evidence: This is inferred from the FRET efficiency values being lower than the IF1 state.

claim: The presence of multiple apo states underscores the conformational flexibility of MRP1 in the absence of ligand.
source: The presence of multiple apo states underscores the conformational flexibility of MRP1 in the absence of ligand, a well-documented characteristic of many ABC transporters (Husada et al., 2018; Timachi et al., 2017; Ward et al., 2007; Ward et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of multiple IF states and is supported by literature on other ABC transporters.

claim: In the cryo-EM structure of apo bMRP1, the local resolution of the NBDs was poorer compared to other regions, suggesting that the NBDs are relatively mobile.
source: In the cryo-EM structure of apo bMRP1, the local resolution of the NBDs was poorer compared to other regions, suggesting that the NBDs are relatively mobile (Johnson and Chen, 2017).
evidence: This is an observation from prior cryo-EM work that supports the conformational flexibility of the NBDs.

claim: In the absence of ATP, the vast majority of transitions occurred among the four IF states (IF1, IF2, IF3, and IF4).
source: In the absence of ATP, the vast majority of transitions occurred among the four IF states (IF1, IF2, IF3, and IF4) (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from analysis of smFRET trajectories shown in Figure 3A and supplementary figures.

claim: The lifetime of each IF state was on average around 1 s.
source: The lifetime of each IF state was on average around 1 s (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from smFRET data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Addition of LTC4 increased the lifetime of IF1 by about 30%.
source: Addition of LTC4 increased the lifetime of IF1 by about 30%, lending further support to its assignment as the substrate-bound state, whereas ATP did not produce statistically significant changes in the lifetime of any IF state (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from smFRET data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: ATP did not produce statistically significant changes in the lifetime of any IF state.
source: Addition of LTC4 increased the lifetime of IF1 by about 30%, lending further support to its assignment as the substrate-bound state, whereas ATP did not produce statistically significant changes in the lifetime of any IF state (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from smFRET data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Increasing the ATP concentration from 10 µM to 5 mM shortened twait by approximately twofold.
source: Increasing the ATP concentration from 10 µM to 5 mM shortened twait by approximately twofold (Figure 4C), consistent with the understanding that ATP binding promotes NBD dimerization.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from perturbation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The presence of LTC4 reduced twait at both limiting and saturating ATP concentrations.
source: The presence of LTC4 reduced twait at both limiting and saturating ATP concentrations (Figure 4C), indicating that substrate accelerates the transition from the IF to OF state.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from perturbation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Substrate accelerates the transition from the IF to OF state.
source: The presence of LTC4 reduced twait at both limiting and saturating ATP concentrations (Figure 4C), indicating that substrate accelerates the transition from the IF to OF state.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that LTC4 reduces the wait time to the first OF state.

claim: The vast majority of transitions into the OF state originated from IF1 or IF2.
source: Moreover, we found that the vast majority of transitions into the OF state originated from IF1 or IF2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that the substrate-bound configuration IF1 is not an obligatory intermediate en route to the OF state.
evidence: This is a direct observation from transition density plots shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The substrate-bound configuration IF1 is not an obligatory intermediate en route to the OF state.
source: Moreover, we found that the vast majority of transitions into the OF state originated from IF1 or IF2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that the substrate-bound configuration IF1 is not an obligatory intermediate en route to the OF state.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that transitions to OF can occur from both IF1 and IF2.

claim: Increasing the ATP concentration shortened tIF.
source: As expected from the notion that ATP drives the IF-to-OF isomerization, increasing the ATP concentration shortened tIF (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from perturbation experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: LTC4 reduced the average tIF by approximately threefold.
source: LTC4 further reduced the average tIF by approximately threefold (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from perturbation experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In the absence of ATP, spontaneous transitions into the OF state were occasionally observed.
source: In control experiments where the molecules were incubated with buffer or LTC4 alone in the absence of ATP, spontaneous transitions into the OF state were occasionally observed (Figure 5A), but the resultant OF states on average only lasted a few seconds (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In the absence of ATP, the resultant OF states on average only lasted a few seconds.
source: In control experiments where the molecules were incubated with buffer or LTC4 alone in the absence of ATP, spontaneous transitions into the OF state were occasionally observed (Figure 5A), but the resultant OF states on average only lasted a few seconds (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The average OF lifetime measured in the presence of saturating ATP was longer than 20 s.
source: In comparison, the average OF lifetime measured in the presence of saturating ATP was longer than 20 s (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that ATP stabilizes the OF conformation.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: ATP stabilizes the OF conformation.
source: In comparison, the average OF lifetime measured in the presence of saturating ATP was longer than 20 s (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that ATP stabilizes the OF conformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ATP increases the OF state lifetime.

claim: LTC4 had only a minor effect on the kinetics of OF-to-IF transitions.
source: LTC4 had only a minor effect on the kinetics of OF-to-IF transitions (Figure 5B and Table 1), consistent with the structural observation that LTC4 is readily released in the ATP-bound OF conformation prior to ATP hydrolysis (Johnson and Chen, 2018), hence not affecting the subsequent isomerization back to the IF state.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from smFRET experiments shown in Figure 5B and Table 1.

claim: LTC4 is readily released in the ATP-bound OF conformation prior to ATP hydrolysis.
source: LTC4 had only a minor effect on the kinetics of OF-to-IF transitions (Figure 5B and Table 1), consistent with the structural observation that LTC4 is readily released in the ATP-bound OF conformation prior to ATP hydrolysis (Johnson and Chen, 2018), hence not affecting the subsequent isomerization back to the IF state.
evidence: This is a structural observation from prior work cited in the manuscript.

claim: When saturating concentrations of ATP and LTC4 were present, the transition from the OF to the IF conformation was much slower than the IF-to-OF transition.
source: When saturating concentrations of ATP and LTC4 were present, the transition from the OF to the IF conformation was much slower than the IF-to-OF transition (tOF vs. tIF, Table 1), also evident from the single-molecule trajectories (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct comparison of measured lifetimes shown in Table 1 and Figure 4A.

claim: Under physiological conditions where ATP is saturating, MRP1 spends the majority of its time in the OF conformation.
source: Therefore, it is likely that under physiological conditions where ATP is saturating, MRP1 spends the majority of its time in the OF conformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that tOF is much longer than tIF at saturating ATP.

claim: The total cycle time measured from the single-molecule data (tOF + tIF) is 4–6 times longer than that deduced from the bulk ATPase assay.
source: The total cycle time measured from the single-molecule data (tOF + tIF, Table 1) is 4–6 times longer than that deduced from the bulk ATPase assay (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct comparison between smFRET and bulk ATPase measurements.

claim: The temperature differed between the smFRET and bulk ATPase assays (23°C for smFRET vs. 30°C for bulk assay).
source: The temperature differed between the two assays (23°C for smFRET vs. 30°C for bulk assay).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: Surface immobilization of MRP1 may affect its activity.
source: It is also possible that surface immobilization of MRP1 may affect its activity.
evidence: This is speculation about potential experimental artifacts.

claim: Some fast transitions between IF and OF states may escape detection at the 300 ms time resolution of smFRET measurements.
source: Finally, some fast transitions between IF and OF states may escape detection at the 300 ms time resolution of smFRET measurements.
evidence: This is speculation about potential limitations of the experimental technique.

claim: Based on the smFRET data, most particles would adopt an OF conformation in the presence of saturating LTC4 and ATP.
source: Based on the smFRET data (Figures 2A and 4A), we anticipated that most particles would adopt an OF conformation in the presence of saturating LTC4 and ATP.
evidence: This is a prediction based on prior smFRET observations.

claim: If ATP hydrolysis were rate limiting, the predominant species would be the pre-hydrolysis state with ATP molecules bound at both ATPase sites.
source: Further, if ATP hydrolysis were rate limiting, the predominant species would be the pre-hydrolysis state with ATP molecules bound at both ATPase sites.
evidence: This is a hypothetical prediction to test the rate-limiting step.

claim: If ATP hydrolysis is not rate limiting, the predominant structure would be one in which ATP in the catalytically competent, consensus site has already been hydrolyzed.
source: Otherwise, we would expect to observe a dominant structure in which ATP in the catalytically competent, consensus site has already been hydrolyzed.
evidence: This is a hypothetical prediction to test the rate-limiting step.

claim: The cryo-EM reconstruction at 3.4 Å shows an NBD-dimerized conformation, with an ATP molecule in the degenerate site and an ADP molecule in the consensus site.
source: Consistent with the single-molecule data, the resulting map shows an NBD-dimerized conformation, with an ATP molecule in the degenerate site and an ADP molecule in the consensus site (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The higher quality cryo-EM map at 3.2 Å unambiguously shows an ADP molecule at the consensus site.
source: To improve the resolution of the structure, we also carried out 3D classification and obtained a higher quality map at 3.2 Å from a subset of the particles (Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2), which unambiguously shows an ADP molecule at the consensus site (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 6.

claim: The cryo-EM structure strongly suggests that ATP hydrolysis is a fast step in the transport cycle.
source: This structure strongly suggests that ATP hydrolysis is a fast step in the transport cycle, whereas dissociation of the NBD dimer constitutes a kinetic bottleneck, thereby limiting the rate of the overall cycle.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the predominant structure under active turnover has ADP in the consensus site.

claim: Dissociation of the NBD dimer constitutes a kinetic bottleneck, thereby limiting the rate of the overall cycle.
source: This structure strongly suggests that ATP hydrolysis is a fast step in the transport cycle, whereas dissociation of the NBD dimer constitutes a kinetic bottleneck, thereby limiting the rate of the overall cycle.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the predominant structure under active turnover has ADP in the consensus site, indicating that the post-hydrolysis state accumulates.

claim: Other than ADP occupying the consensus site in place of ATP, the overall structure of the post-hydrolysis conformation is essentially identical to that of the pre-hydrolytic structure solved with the hydrolysis-deficient E1454Q mutant.
source: Other than ADP occupying the consensus site in place of ATP, the overall structure of this post-hydrolysis conformation is essentially identical to that of the pre-hydrolytic structure solved with the hydrolysis-deficient E1454Q mutant (Johnson and Chen, 2018; Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is a direct comparison of cryo-EM structures shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: In both the post-hydrolysis and pre-hydrolytic structures, the intracellular gate is closed and the substrate-binding site is pulled apart such that LTC4 is no longer bound.
source: In both structures, the intracellular gate is closed and the substrate-binding site is pulled apart such that LTC4 is no longer bound.
evidence: This is a direct observation from comparing cryo-EM structures.

claim: For MRP1, ATP hydrolysis per se and the subsequent release of inorganic phosphate (Pi) do not induce conformational rearrangements.
source: Thus, for MRP1, ATP hydrolysis per se and the subsequent release of inorganic phosphate (Pi) do not induce conformational rearrangements.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the pre- and post-hydrolysis structures are essentially identical.

claim: MRP1 is intrinsically dynamic, transitioning between multiple IF conformations both in the absence and presence of ATP.
source: By monitoring the separation of the two NBDs, we showed that MRP1 is intrinsically dynamic: in the absence of any ligand, MRP1 transitions among multiple IF conformations.
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments.

claim: MRP1 spontaneously accesses the OF conformation, albeit with lower frequency and shorter lifetime in the absence of nucleotides.
source: It also spontaneously accesses the OF conformation, albeit with lower frequency and shorter lifetime in the absence of nucleotides.
evidence: This is a direct observation from smFRET experiments.

claim: A recent smFRET study showed that the E. coli peptide transporter McjD also samples an NBD-dimerized state without nucleotides.
source: Similarly, a recent smFRET study showed that the E. coli peptide transporter McjD also samples an NBD-dimerized state without nucleotides (Husada et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a citation of prior work on another ABC transporter.

claim: When ATP is present, the MRP1 transport cycle is a nonequilibrium process coupled to ATP hydrolysis.
source: When ATP is present, as in physiological conditions, the MRP1 transport cycle is a nonequilibrium process coupled to ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a general statement about the thermodynamics of active transport.

claim: ATP binding accelerates the IF-to-OF transition (k1) and slows down the reverse OF-to-IF transition (k-1) by stabilizing the OF conformation.
source: ATP binding accelerates the IF-to-OF transition (k1) and slows down the reverse OF-to-IF transition (k-1) by stabilizing the OF conformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the smFRET measurements of IF and OF lifetimes under different ATP concentrations.

claim: Substrate, such as LTC4, stimulates the ATPase activity through acceleration of the IF-to-OF transition (k1), but not ATP hydrolysis (k2) or the subsequent OF-to-IF transition (k3).
source: Substrate, such as LTC4, stimulates the ATPase activity through acceleration of the IF-to-OF transition (k1), but not ATP hydrolysis (k2) or the subsequent OF-to-IF transition (k3).
evidence: This is inferred from the smFRET measurements showing that LTC4 reduces tIF but not tOF.

claim: The same high FRET value (E = 0.92) is produced by two distinct NBD-dimerized states: the pre-hydrolytic state in which two ATP molecules are bound and an asymmetric post-hydrolytic state bound with one ATP and one ADP.
source: In this model, the same high FRET value (E = 0.92) is produced by two distinct NBD-dimerized states: the pre-hydrolytic state in which two ATP molecules are bound and an asymmetric post-hydrolytic state bound with one ATP and one ADP.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of smFRET and cryo-EM data.

claim: The lifetime distributions of the E = 0.92 state can be fit with single-exponential decay functions.
source: Still, the lifetime distributions of the E = 0.92 state can be fit with single-exponential decay functions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating a single slow step governing the OF lifetime.
evidence: This is a direct observation from fitting the OF lifetime distributions shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: ATP hydrolysis (k2) is a fast step followed by a comparatively slow NBD dissociation step (k3).
source: This is probably because ATP hydrolysis (k2) is a fast step followed by a comparatively slow NBD dissociation step (k3).
evidence: This is inferred from the single-exponential decay of OF lifetimes and the cryo-EM structure showing ADP in the consensus site.

claim: At physiological ATP concentrations (1–10 mM), the rate-limiting step is the dissociation of the NBD dimer subsequent to ATP hydrolysis.
source: The cryo-EM data further support that at physiological ATP concentrations (1–10 mM), the rate-limiting step is the dissociation of the NBD dimer subsequent to ATP hydrolysis (Figure 7).
evidence: This is inferred from the cryo-EM structure showing the post-hydrolysis state as the predominant species.

claim: Recent studies of P-glycoprotein, TmrAB, and TM287/288 also indicated that in their respective transport cycles, the OF-to-IF transition is rate limiting.
source: Recent studies of P-glycoprotein (Bársony et al., 2016), TmrAB (Hofmann et al., 2019), and TM287/288 (Hutter et al., 2019) also indicated that in their respective transport cycles, the OF-to-IF transition is rate limiting.
evidence: This is a citation of prior work on other ABC transporters.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of MRP1 shows that the ATP hydrolysis step per se does not induce any conformational change.
source: The cryo-EM structure of MRP1 shows that the ATP hydrolysis step per se does not induce any conformational change (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct observation from comparing pre- and post-hydrolysis cryo-EM structures shown in Figure 6.

claim: Thermodynamically, the energy provided by ATP hydrolysis is necessary for uphill substrate translocation.
source: Thermodynamically, the energy provided by ATP hydrolysis is necessary for uphill substrate translocation.
evidence: This is a general principle of active transport based on thermodynamics.

claim: Without energy dissipation, the system can only reach equilibrium, in which the substrate concentration is equal on both sides of the membrane.
source: Without energy dissipation, the system can only reach equilibrium, in which the substrate concentration is equal on both sides of the membrane.
evidence: This is a general principle of thermodynamics.

claim: Kinetically, ATP hydrolysis provides directionality to the transport cycle.
source: Kinetically, ATP hydrolysis provides directionality to the transport cycle: because k2 is much greater than the reverse isomerization rate k-1, estimated from the E1454Q cycling traces (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), the majority of molecules proceed to ATP hydrolysis upon NBD dimerization, followed by isomerization back to the IF conformation with a rate of k3.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of rate constants measured from WT and E1454Q mutant.

claim: k2 is much greater than the reverse isomerization rate k-1.
source: Kinetically, ATP hydrolysis provides directionality to the transport cycle: because k2 is much greater than the reverse isomerization rate k-1, estimated from the E1454Q cycling traces (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), the majority of molecules proceed to ATP hydrolysis upon NBD dimerization, followed by isomerization back to the IF conformation with a rate of k3.
evidence: This is estimated from the E1454Q cycling traces shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The E1454Q mutant displayed transitions between IF and OF conformations with kinetics similar to the WT transporter.
source: Although the E1454Q mutant is catalytically deficient, it displayed transitions between IF and OF conformations with kinetics similar to the WT transporter (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct comparison of measured lifetimes shown in Table 1.
